name: Field Doctor-Style Chicken Tikka Masala (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
630 g Chicken
505 g Whole grain rice
1 1/4 x 400 g tins Plum Tomato
160 g Broccoli
160 g Spinach
160 g Chickpeas
3/4 Red Peppers
80 g Soy Milk [SOY beans, water]
70 g Coconut Milk [Coconut, Water]
70 g Red Quinoa
1 1/2 tbsp Ginger
1/3 Lemon Juice
1 1/2 tsp Tomato Puree [tomato]
1 tbsp Coriander
1 tsp Tapioca Starch
2/3 tsp Sweet Noble Paprika
1/3 tsp Brown Sugar
1/4 tsp Chicken Stock (Chicken Extract, Chicken Fat, Salt], Turmeric Blend, Cumin seeds (whole), Garam Masala, Fennel Ground, Sea Salt, Chilli Powder, Black Pepper
directions:
1. Grains: Cook wholegrain rice and red quinoa; drain and keep warm.

2. Spice base: Warm extra virgin olive oil with ginger, cumin seeds, turmeric, garam masala, fennel, sweet paprika, chilli powder and black pepper.

3. Sauce: Add chopped tomato, tomato puree, soy milk, coconut milk, lemon juice, brown sugar and chicken stock. Simmer into a masala sauce; thicken with tapioca slurry if needed.

4. Chicken & veg: Brown diced chicken, then simmer in the sauce with broccoli, chickpeas and red pepper until chicken is cooked. Fold in spinach. Season with salt. Finish with coriander. Serve over rice–quinoa.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.
description:
Ingredients: Water, Chicken, Whole grain rice, Chopped Tomato, Broccoli, Spinach, Chickpeas, Red Pepper...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Chicken Tikka Masala (Low FODMAP) (~416 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/chicken-tikka-masala-low-fodmap
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~416 g x 8 = 3328 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~628 g (inferred ~18.88% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~49 g (inferred ~1.48% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
